title: Capacity fidelity covenant: SLA quantification, error-budget cadence, and autoscale interlock language
creator: Maya Chen
description: Purpose: Define a compact, measurable SLA and accompanying error-budget cadence for Dedicated capacity customers that (1) sets clear per-customer obligations, (2) ties autoscale behavior to contractual remediation, and (3) provides unambiguous credit computation language for billing/legal. Scope: SLA metric definitions (serve-rate and p95 latency bands), error-budget accrual and burn windows, autoscale interlock triggers and observable bindings, and two contract clause variants (standard and enterprise). Deliverables: final SLA spec doc, example contract paragraph snippets, PromQL/metrics bindings for verification, and a one-page customer-facing explainer. Acceptance criteria listed below.
acceptance_criteria: Numeric SLA definitions for at least two guarantee tiers (Baseline, Premium) expressed in quantiles and units (tokens/minute, requests/sec, p95 latency)
Error-budget computation described as a rolling 7-day window with daily reconciliation and explicit burn rules for transient incidents
Clear autoscale interlock: when measured serve-rate falls below 80% of committed baseline for >10 minutes, automatic shift to mitigation routing and start of credit calculation
Contract language snippets reviewed by Legal and Security and inserted into contract templates
Monitoring queries and Grafana dashboard links included and validated with sample dataset and test harness
contract_clauses: Service Commitment: Redwood Inference will provide Dedicated Capacity aligned to the Customer's Committed Serve Rate (CSR). CSR is measured as tokens-per-minute (TPM) averaged per AZ and reported on a rolling 7-day window. If actual sustained CSR falls below 90% of the Commit for a billing window, the Customer is eligible for service credits as defined below.

Autoscale Interlock & Mitigation: When observed CSR for the Customer drops below 80% of CSR for 10 consecutive minutes, Redwood will (a) initiate mitigation routing to compatible model variants, (b) open a priority incident to the Customer workspace, and (c) start error-budget reconciliation. These mitigations are considered operational actions and do not affect the Customer's entitlement to credits unless they are successful in restoring CSR above threshold within 60 minutes.

Credit Computation: Service credit = min(30%, ((Committed - Measured)/Committed) * 100%) pro-rated by duration. Credit windows are computed daily over the 7-day rolling period and capped per billing month. Credits are applied as a percentage of the monthly Dedicated fee and do not include usage-based overage charges.

Force Majeure & Maintenance: Planned maintenance windows >24 hours are prenotified and do not count toward credits. Outages attributable to Customer-provided infra or misconfiguration are excluded. All other exceptions are subject to arbitration per Section X.
error_budget_spec: Error budget is defined as the complement of the SLA meet-rate over a rolling 7-day window. Meet-rate is computed at 5-minute resolution as 'served_units' / 'committed_units' per AZ, per customer. Daily reconciliation aggregates minute-level misses and applies a decay to old misses (exponential window with alpha=0.2) to prioritize recent regressions. Burn events: any contiguous block where meet-rate < 0.8 triggers an incident-level burn that is counted separately and weighted at 1.5x for credit calculation.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal pilot): apply language and monitoring to three existing Dedicated customers; run parallel measurement for two weeks without applying credits. Phase 2 (soft launch): notify pilot customers, enable crediting for one billing cycle with capped exposure. Phase 3 (GA): roll into standard contract language and product billing flow. Key checkpoints: Legal sign-off, Billing integration QA, Observability end-to-end verification.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Measurement drift between internal metrics and customer-facing reports. Mitigation: publish canonical PromQL and a reconciliation job that runs nightly and emits a signed report
Risk: Excessive credit exposure on GA. Mitigation: soft-launch cap (max 15% of monthly fees) and staged removal during first 3 months

Risk: Autoscale mitigations change request behavior and create customer surprise. Mitigation: include explicit autoscale behavior section in the customer explainer and an opt-out for highly regulated customers
